title: A novel role for EZH2 in A-to-I RNA editing in prostate cancer
text:
EZH2 is a well-known histone lysine methyltransferase and an oncogene upregulated in many types of
cancer, including prostate cancer. In this project, we will investigate the novel noncanonical, Polycomb-
repressive complex-independent role for EZH2 in A-to-I RNA editing via ADAR. Successful completion of this
project will provide novel mechanistic insights EZH2’s novel functions beyond its lysine methyltransferase and
transcription repressor activities.

title: Retinal neurovascular protection by boosting efferocytosis
text:
Myeloid cells (microglia and macrophages) can contribute to both tissue injury and repair in retinal diseases.
Efferocytosis, a reparative aspect of myeloid cells by which they “eat” and thereby clean up dead cells, is well-
studied in some disease conditions, but whether efferocytosis alleviates retinopathy and how this occurs is poorly
understood. This proposal is designed to identify new mechanisms involved in efferocytosis with a potential to
develop new therapeutic strategies for retinopathies associated with ischemia and trauma.

title: Epicardial regulation of cardiomyocyte function via modulation of extracellular signals: toward a model of human muscle pump function
text:
This work will bolster our understanding of epicardial-myocardial signaling and the role of the extracellular matrix
in modulating cell behavior in the developing heart. The clinical relevance of this work lies in the application of
epicardial cells to enhance the pump function of a perfusable, chambered, human cardiac tissue model that will
be ideal to study the impact of cardiac disease and therapeutics on pressure-volume dynamics, stroke work, and
ejection fraction. In the future, this living, human muscle pump generated in a dish might be used to restore
cardiac function in patients with heart disease.

title: Molecular Consequences of Sex Chromosome Copy Number Variation
text:
Men and women have distinct genetic makeups that affect their development, health, and disease risk,
but the underlying biological mechanisms remain unclear. We previously identified a list of candidate
genes on the X and Y chromosomes that differ in expression between males and females and may
underlie these biological differences. Beginning with a key pair of these genes that regulate thousands
of other genes, we propose to investigate their biochemical properties, evolutionary history, and impact
on gene activity in male and female cells, leading to a better understanding of human biology and new
prevention and therapeutic strategies effective for both sexes.

title: Calcium Nanoparticles to Enhance Immuno-Radiotherapy
text:
This project aims to investigate anti-CD205 antibody-conjugated calcium nanoparticles as a novel type of
immunomodulator. It is hypothesized that the nanoparticles can selectively increase the cytosolic calcium levels
of circulating dendritic cells, thereby enhancing their tumor infiltration and antigen cross-presentation. These
nanoparticles are expected to effectively enhance radio-immunotherapy.

title: DNA methylation epimutations in leukemia
text:
DNA methylation is a chemical modification of DNA that is essential for normal tissue development and is altered
in nearly all cancers for reasons that are poorly understood. We recently discovered that acute myeloid leukemia
cells contain thousands of patient-specific DNA methylation changes on only one copy of the genome, which
can pre-exist in normal blood stem cells and affect the expression of leukemia-related genes. This project will
define the genomic landscape of these allele-specific DNA methylation “epimutations” in leukemia and explore
their contribution to leukemia development and utility as biomarkers for predicting of disease progression and
relapse in leukemia patients.

title: Research Education
text: PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT- RESEARCH EDUCATION CORE The Research Education Core (REC) of the H-H U54 is committed to advancing cancer research education at Howard University (HU) and strengthening the national cancer research workforce. Building on the longstanding collaboration between HU and Johns Hopkins University (JHU), the Core will implement integrated research and educational programs that leverage the complementary strengths of both institutions. Key initiatives include the establishment of a joint Ph.D. program in Medical Physics, the implementation of the “School2Lab” initiative to engage rising junior and senior STEM students from regional high schools, and the development of innovative coursework focused on the applications of artificial intelligence and machine learning in cancer research and education. These initiatives will be delivered through the Research Opportunity and Innovation at Johns Hopkins and Howard Universities (ROI@J-HU) training framework, which supports structured mentorship, early research engagement, and cross-institution collaboration. Collectively, these efforts aim to expand access to advanced training in oncology and biomedical sciences, while preparing a skilled and well-equipped workforce to address emerging challenges in cancer research and care.

title: A machine learning computational approach for developing synchronized EEG and behavior biomarkers in young autistic children
text: ABSTRACT – Project 3 The overall goal of the Duke Autism Center of Excellence is to use a translational digital health and computational approach to address the critical need for more effective autism screening tools, objective outcome measures, and brain-based biomarkers that can be used in clinical trials with young autistic children. Despite significant advances in understanding the biological basis of autism, clinical trials continue to rely on subjective clinical observation and caregiver report measures. Objective, biologically based biomarkers are needed for use in clinical trials that can parse heterogeneity, assess target engagement, and monitor outcomes. Autism biomarker studies have utilized electroencephalography (EEG) and eye-tracking measures, which have found differences between autistic and neurotypical individuals in neural and attentional processing of social stimuli. However, to date, the majority of autism biomarker studies have used independent experimental paradigms and separate analyses of EEG and gaze. Technical and computational advances, including machine learning and computer vision analysis, now allow for synchronized measurement and analysis of EEG and behavior, including eye- tracking, each of which provides distinct sources of information that can be integrated to improve biomarker performance. Project 3 will use an innovative machine learning computational method to develop a multimodal biomarker that combines features of EEG activity and synchronized measures of children’s behavior (e.g., social attention) automatically coded via computer vision analysis. We will test the hypothesis that a multimodal biomarker will show enhanced discrimination between autistic and neurotypical children compared to biomarkers based on EEG alone. Standard and novel methods will be used to combine synchronized behavior (digital phenotypes) and EEG features, with a focus on neural connectivity measured via traditional methods (coherence, phase-lag index) and new network analysis methods (discriminative cross-spectral factor analysis) developed by our team. This multimodal approach will be evaluated in 3–6-year-old autistic children without intellectual disability (ID), age- and sex-matched neurotypical children, and autistic children with ID (IQ <= 70). Multimodal biomarkers will be compared to three commonly used EEG biomarkers. Our goal is to develop robust, brain-based biomarkers that can be used in clinical trials to evaluate early interventions for young autistic children designed to improve outcomes and quality of life.

title: Investigating pulmonary complications due to abnormal collagen/ER stress in Osteogenesis Imperfecta
text:
Pulmonary complications are the leading cause of mortality in patients with osteogenesis imperfecta (OI) and
the mechanisms behind these complications, specifically reaction to environmental damage, are unknown and
not well explored. This proposal will gain insights into the mechanisms causing OI lung insufficiency and
completion of the aims will contribute to knowledge regarding the effect of abnormal extracellular matrix
secretion and ER stress on lung cell differentiation and damage recovery as well as the effect of in vivo ER
stress inhibition treatment. Importantly, our study will identify novel targets for future clinical therapies that
could ameliorate OI lung abnormalities, for which there are presently no established treatments.

title: Machine Learning Approaches for Analyzing Microbiome Dynamics in Ventilator-Associated Pneumonia
text:
Ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) affects up to 50% of mechanically ventilated patients but lacks
accurate diagnostic methods, leading to delayed treatment and increased healthcare costs. This project
develops machine learning approaches integrating longitudinal microbiome data with clinical parameters to
identify microbial patterns that predict VAP development earlier than current methods. The research advances
computational microbiome analysis while training undergraduate students in interdisciplinary data science
applied to critical clinical challenges.

title: Rapid Culture-Independent Detection of Sepsis Causing Microorganism Directly from Blood
text:
Sepsis is a rapid-developing and life-threatening condition caused by the body’s extreme reaction to an infection.
Early detection of sepsis-causing agents enables precise treatment and higher chance of survival for patients,
but current molecular diagnostic technologies still depend on lengthy blood culture. This MIRA project aims to
develop a blood culture-independent sensing device to accurately detect sepsis-causing pathogens in about 2
hours after blood sampling.

title: Integrating Loneliness and Social Isolation Insights into Late-Life Suicide Risk Prediction Through the Digital Phenotyping of Electronic Health Records
text:
(PUBLIC HEALTH RELEVANCE)
This study addresses the problem of predicting late-life suicide risk among older adults, driven by loneliness and
social isolation, by utilizing the latest artificial intelligence and natural language processing methods. Existing
risk assessment approaches often neglect these social factors, encapsulated in free text format, and underutilize
longitudinal electronic health record (EHR) data. The overarching goal is to enhance suicide risk predictions and
improve EHR data use, enabling more accurate assessments, timely interventions, and personalized care for
lonely and socially isolated older adults.

title: Cochlear neuron functions and diseases
text:
Work from our laboratory has revealed how sensory hair cells and neurons in the cochlea coordinate and
regulate their electrical and biochemical tools necessary to confer hearing mechanisms. We propose
investigating how the neurons that process information from the lion's share of hair cells relay sensory
information to the brain in health and disease states.

title: Identifying complex modes of adaptation from population-genomic data
text:
Natural selection is an important evolutionary force that enables humans to adapt to new environments and fight
disease-causing pathogens. However, the unique footprints of natural selection in our genome can be buried
beneath those left by other evolutionary forces. Thus, by leveraging information about multiple evolutionary
forces, we can identify signatures of natural selection in the human genome, and ultimately determine its role in
human adaptation and disease.

title: The electrical basis of proprioceptive signaling
text:
Project Narrative. Proprioception is the ability to internally sense limb position and posture and is encoded by
sensory neurons called proprioceptors, which transform changes in muscle length and force into electrical
signals that are transmitted to locomotor circuits in the spinal cord. Normal proprioceptor function is essential for
purposeful movement and is impaired in a variety of conditions, including spinal cord injury, aging, and
amyotrophic lateral sclerosis; however, little is known about how electrical signals in proprioceptors are sent.
This research will enhance scientific understanding of mammalian proprioception by systematically defining how
voltage-gated sodium channels (NaVs) differentially shape proprioceptive signaling in the healthy nervous
system, with important implications for understanding and ultimately treating conditions in which proprioception
is impaired.

title: An Innovative Approach to Identify Correctors of Metabolic Complications in HIV
text:
Metabolic and cardiovascular complications of HIV and antiretroviral therapy are leading causes of premature
aging associated with long-term HIV disease. This proposal will use advanced strategies for high-throughput
screening and subsequent chemical optimization to identify and characterize novel highly selective chemical
probes to a validated therapeutic target that has so far proven challenging, despite strong rationale. Altogether,
this proposal aims to address the significant unmet clinical need for new and more effective therapies to
ameliorate HIV- and ART-associated metabolic complications.

title: Single nucleus gene expression in moderate and compulsive drug self-administration in a rodent model of HIV
text:
The molecular mechanisms responsible for neuropsychological impairment in HIV patients are not easily inferred
with conventional high-throughput analysis methods. To investigate the molecular mechanisms behind the
interactions of HIV and methamphetamine (METH), this interdisciplinary project will profile gene expression at
the single cell level in key brain regions relevant to the effects of persistent HIV infection and substance use
disorder (SUD) in a small animal model of neuroHIV in a behavioral paradigm of voluntary intravenous METH
self-administration. We will bring to bear computational methods to elucidate the genes (master regulator genes)
driving the altered gene expression, which will provide a framework for new testable hypotheses on the
mechanisms underlying the neuropathogenesis of the increased neuroinflammation, neurodegeneration and
compulsivity to take METH in the context of METH abuse that can be targeted therapeutically to improve
neuropsychological functioning in people with HIV.

title: PKR sensing of mitochondrial dsRNA in childhood Sjogrens disease
text:
This project is to determine molecular mechanisms of cytoplasmic mitochondrial double-stranded RNA (dsRNA)
sensing by PKR in children with autoimmune Sjӧgren’s disease. The investigation of immune cell gene signatures
and target tissue inflammation affected by dsRNA will potentially offer diagnostic and therapeutic targets in this rare
cohort.

title: Cellular and Molecular Imaging Core
text:
Program Director/Principal Investigator (Last, First, Middle): Michael A. Webster
 PROJECT NARRATIVE
Cellular and Molecular Imaging Core
Modern neuroscience research requires access to newly emerging technologies and instruments that are often
difficult and impractical to support in individual laboratories. Building on its successful operation and support of
outstanding investigators at the University of Nevada, Reno (UNR), the COBRE Cellular and Molecular Imaging
(CMI) core facility seeks continued funding to transition to a sustainable core to provide support to COBRE
faculty investigators and others with an emphasis in gaining fundamental knowledge about the basic function,
development and disorders of the nervous system.
